entry.summary: ESTA under the Visa Waiver Program for tourism or business visits under 90 days. No paid or unpaid work, including volunteering, house-sitting or pet-sitting.
entry.max_stay: Under 90 days; the date on your I-94 record is the one that counts
entry.pre_arrival: Apply for ESTA. Be ready to answer questions about purpose, length, where you'll stay and your ties to Australia; officers may inspect devices and social media.
entry.other: A refused ESTA, a past refusal of entry or a stay over 90 days needs a visa interview at a US Embassy or Consulate in Australia. Some visa types require public social media settings. An onward ticket can't end in Canada, Mexico or the Caribbean unless you live there.

laws.rule: Federal and state laws for drug-related offences vary, including laws related to the possession and recreational and/or medical use of marijuana (cannabis). Penalties for drug-related offences can be severe and often include minimum mandatory sentences. Some medications readily available in Australia are illegal or considered controlled substances in the US, even if prescribed by an Australian doctor. It's also illegal to possess any prescription medication without a prescription. See Health. US Customs and Border Protection (CBP) - Travelling with Medication

laws.rule: The federal legal age for buying and drinking alcohol is 21 years old. State laws regarding the possession and consumption of alcohol can vary. Check the relevant state laws.

laws.rule: No federal law explicitly protects LGBTQIA+ people from discrimination, and not all state and local non-discrimination laws include protections based on sexual orientation or gender identity. Some states and localities have laws that may discriminate against or otherwise affect LGBTQIA+ travellers. Check relevant state and local laws. Although Australian passports comply with international standards for sex and gender, we can't guarantee that a passport showing 'X' in the sex field will be accepted for entry or transit by another country. Contact the nearest United States Embassy or Consulate before you travel for further information.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the United States Dollar (USD). Declare all amounts over USD 10,000 (or its foreign equivalent) on arrival and departure. This covers all forms of currency, not only US dollars and not only cash. Failing to do so is a serious violation which can result in the seizure and forfeiture of your money. Criminal penalties can also apply. Banks and ATMs are widespread, and currency exchange services are available in most major cities and airports. Major credit cards are almost universally accepted. culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: On public lands (National Park Service): follow the seven Leave No Trace principles (plan ahead, stay on durable surfaces, dispose of waste properly, leave what you find, minimise campfire impacts, respect wildlife, be considerate of others). Watch wildlife from a distance and never feed it.
culture-and-protocol.sacred_or_restricted_places: At archaeological and sacred places, stay on marked trails. Don't touch, dig, remove or alter artefacts or rock art. Honour requests for quiet and privacy; many sites are sacred to Tribal Nations, who are their cultural authority.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: National Park Service; the Tribal Nation for each site.
culture-and-protocol.note: From federal government guidance; there is no single national etiquette page.

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: No public directory of drone pilots; the FAA Airmen Inquiry can verify a named pilot's certificate. Commercial flying needs a Part 107 Remote Pilot Certificate; foreign operators also need a DOT foreign aircraft permit. National parks publish public-domain b-roll.

register.name: FAA Airmen Inquiry (verifies a named certificate holder; not a directory)

items.text: There is no public directory of Part 107 pilots to browse; the FAA Airmen Inquiry lets you search a named person's airman certificate to verify it.
Part 107 operations need an FAA Remote Pilot Certificate with a small UAS rating, from a knowledge test taken at a US testing centre. The FAA does not recognise any foreign remote pilot certificate.

A foreign civil drone flown for compensation needs a DOT foreign aircraft permit (14 CFR Part 375, OST Form 4509, at least 15 days ahead, about 30 days in practice). Without a US certificate you may fly only under direct supervision of a US-certificated remote pilot in command, or hire one to fly for you.
Many National Park Service parks publish public-domain b-roll, including aerials (for example Grand Canyon's b-roll index).
